newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian inflation up slightly at 24.6 pct in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian inflation up slightly at 24.6 pct in Oct.

text.p: Nigeria's consumer price inflation rose to 24.6 percent in October this year from 23.7 percent in September, according to government figures released on Friday.
The federal office of statistics, which announced the figures did not say what was responsible for the slight jump.
It said the composite food index for the month actually fell 2.4 percent from the previous month.

"Many price collection centres witnessed improved food supply of many farm produce from the current farm harvest," it said, adding that "Also, the prices of processed food items fell in most of the centres."
Inflation, which was above 70 percent in December last year, has been within the military government's target zone of 20-30 percent set in its 1996 fiscal budget since June this year.

The government says war on inflation is the goal of a tight fiscal policy that has persisted from 1995 through the 1996 budget. The policy has stabilised various sectors of the economy but has yet to induce real growth.

Central Bank governor Paul Ogwuma said in an interview published on Thursday that reflationary policies would be introduced in next year's budget to try to achieve a growth rate in the gross domestic product of between five to 7.5 percent.
"Having achieved economic stability, we expect the economy to grow in 1997," Ogwuma told the independent Thisday newspaper, adding "I would expect us to grow between five and 7.5 percent."
Nigeria recorded a growth rate of only 2.2 percent last year which experts said was actually negative given its population growth rate of 2.9 percent.
An economic growth rate of about four percent is expected this year.
